sections.h2: How does the new inspection rule change a Southfield sale?
sections.html:
Southfield residential sales now run through a point-of-sale inspection, and that step sets the pace of a closing. City Council approved the program in April 2026 as Ordinance 1835, so schedule the inspection before you commit to a closing date.

The city is an inner-ring Detroit suburb in Oakland County, with a July 2025 Census estimate of 76,111 residents. Owners live in just 53.4 percent of housing units, the lowest share among the four cities in the same Census table, so rentals are common.

A seller can go three ways:

  • Agent listing: showings, the buyer's loan and the city inspection all stack up on the calendar.
  • Private sale: you find the buyer and manage the contract with a title company.
  • Cash sale as-is: the buyer takes the house with whatever the inspection cites. Settle who pays for those repairs before you sign.

Because the program is new, ask the Building Department how it treats a sale that is already under contract, and keep the inspection report with your closing file.

sections.h2: How does the Southfield point-of-sale inspection work?
sections.html:
The Building and Safety Engineering department inspects the house and issues a Certificate of Occupancy after violations are cleared. Its Point of Sale packet walks through the steps, and you apply on the city's online BS&A portal.

  • The packet prints $190 for the resale inspection: $40 to apply, $50 for the certificate and $100 for the building trade, reinspection included.
  • Payment comes first. Staff then book the visit within 14 days of the payment date.
  • A person has to stay at the house for the whole window, either 9:30 to 12:30 or 12:30 to 3:30.
  • Sellers can repair the listed items and ask for a follow-up visit, which the fee covers.
  • Alternatively, buyer and seller both sign an Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations before closing, and the buyer gets 30 days afterward to finish the work.

The affidavit form calls for a performance bond sized to the repairs and bars occupancy until the work passes reinspection. Life safety items must be corrected before anyone moves in. The Building Department answers questions at 248-796-4100.

sections.h2: What is Southfield like for a seller?
sections.html:
Southfield lies about 15 miles northwest of downtown Detroit and holds 26.25 square miles of land. Eight Mile Road bounds it on the south, Inkster Road on the west and Greenfield Road on the east, while the north edge follows roughly Thirteen Mile Road. Lathrup Village, a separate city, sits as an enclave inside the eastern part.

Surveyors laid out the area in 1817 and it became a township in 1830. It incorporated as a city on April 28, 1958, and population jumped from 31,531 in 1960 to 69,298 in 1970. Wikipedia calls it a historic center of mid-century modern architecture in Michigan.

Offices anchor the economy. Wikipedia counts about 27 million square feet of office space and more than 100 Fortune 500 companies with offices here, plus several TV stations and Lawrence Technological University. Northland Center, among the first shopping malls in the country, opened in 1954 and closed in 2015, and its site has been redeveloped as a mixed-use project.

The 2010 census counted 71,739 residents and the 2020 census counted 76,618, so the city grew over the decade. The 2020 median age was 44.0 years, and about 40.9 percent of households were one person living alone.

Southfield City Centre, a mixed-use district near the I-696 and M-10 interchange with offices, a private university and residential neighborhoods, was created in 1992 as a special assessment district. The Civic Center complex, which holds City Hall and the police headquarters, dates to 1964, and an expanded public library opened on its grounds in 2003. Municipal parks and recreation centers were largely built in the 1970s, and Beech Woods Recreation Center and John Grace Community Center are among them.

sections.h2: How can I prepare a Southfield house for the inspection?
sections.html:
Phone the Building Department and ask what the inspector reviews at your address. Check the file for permits that were pulled and never closed out. The packet includes a Furnace / Boiler Certification form with carbon monoxide readings, so a city-registered contractor should service the heating system first.

The 14-day scheduling window only starts after payment, so pay early. Collect your deed, payoff figure and permit records for the title company, and draft the repair affidavit ahead of time if the buyer will take on the work.

Workers average a 23.7 minute trip to work, and 91.9 percent of households have broadband.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads shape a Southfield sale?
sections.html:
Southfield Public Schools runs the city's schools, and Southfield Senior High School for the Arts and Technology has been the only high school since 2015-16, when the two older ones merged. Wikipedia says part of the north sends students to Birmingham and the southeast corner to Oak Park, so confirm a street with the district.

Four routes cross the city: M-10 (the Lodge), I-696, M-39 (the Southfield Freeway) and US-24 (Telegraph). SMART buses cover local and regional lines. The main streets form a one-mile grid, with 9 through 12 Mile Roads east-west and Telegraph, Lahser, Evergreen and Greenfield north-south.

Lawrence Technological University and Oakland Community College are based here.

sections.h2: How does recording work at the Oakland County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Oakland County's Register of Deeds in Pontiac (248-858-0597) takes the deed after the county Treasurer's Office has certified taxes on any warranty deed, warranty-clause deed or land contract. Its recording page also asks for original signatures, a notary acknowledgment on Michigan documents, the buyer's address on the deed and a 2.5 inch top margin on page one.

Call the office for the current recording fee and the county transfer tax rate before you pick a closing date.

sections.h2: What if the Southfield house is vacant or rented?
sections.html:
The Building Department's forms page lists a Rental Registration form, a Vacant Building Registration Application and vacant building owner and purchaser affidavits. Ask which ones apply to your address before you list.

A rented house adds scheduling work, since someone has to be present for the inspection. A vacant house should be secured, heated in cold months and cleared of debris, so the inspector sees its true condition.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection before selling in Southfield?
faqs.a: Yes. Ordinance 1835, approved in April 2026, calls for point-of-sale inspections on residential homes. The packet prints a $190 fee and a Certificate of Occupancy after violations are fixed.

faqs.q: Can the buyer take over the inspector's repair list?
faqs.a: Yes. Both parties sign an Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations before closing. The buyer then has 30 days to finish repairs, and a performance bond is required.

faqs.q: How soon does Southfield schedule the inspection?
faqs.a: Within 14 days of payment. A person must stay at the house through the full morning or afternoon window.

faqs.q: Where do I record a Southfield deed?
faqs.a: Oakland County's Register of Deeds, at 248-858-0597. A warranty deed or land contract needs certification from the county Treasurer's Office before it is recorded.

faqs.q: Does paying cash avoid the Southfield inspection?
faqs.a: No. Point-of-sale rules cover residential sales however they are financed. A cash buyer may take on the cited repairs through the affidavit and keep the closing moving.
